flags.why: Nhơ bẩn is not specifically Northern Vietnamese.
Answers back suggests disrespect, whereas the Vietnamese example praises the girl's quick replies.
flags.fix: The little girl responds very quick-wittedly when talking with adults.

flags.why: Nghĩ quẩn means thinking irrationally out of despair, potentially about self-harm, rather than simply brooding in circles ([dictionary](https://www.rung.vn/dict/vn_vn/Qu%E1%BA%A9n)).
flags.fix: Don't think of doing anything rash; everything will be fine.

flags.why: Chuyển ngữ is a formal term for translating, so the untagged gloss misleadingly presents it as an ordinary conversational verb.
The common use for tangled, overwhelming thoughts or feelings is missing ([dictionary](https://tudientv.com/?t=ng%E1%BB%95n+ngang)).
flags.fix: Add: tangled; confused and overwhelming (of thoughts or feelings).

flags.why: Ná meaning slingshot is primarily Southern usage.
Mẫn cảm is a formal term particularly associated with medical and scientific contexts.
This sense concerns a tight, continuous schedule with no spare time, not promptness or lack of hesitation ([dictionary](https://tudientv.com/?t=s%C3%ADt+sao)).
flags.fix: tightly scheduled; continuous, with no spare time

flags.why: Learners are more likely to encounter sấu as the fruit than as a shortened form of cá sấu.
flags.fix: Put the fruit sense first, the tree sense second, and the crocodile sense third.
